alex_support: Heads-up — customer on dedicated cluster (eu-west1) reporting intermittent 502s and high token latency around 2026-03-16T11:34Z. They provided request ids: req_9a1b2c, req_9a1b2d, req_9a1b2e. Says curl sometimes times out after ~18s. Ticket INC-4821. Can eng/sre help collect node/pod logs + a debug bundle?
priya_sre: Adding context — we've seen a few spikes on that reserved pool last week but no clearOOMs. Need: access logs for those req IDs, pod logs for serve replicas, kubelet/node logs, dmesg, and GPU metrics (nvidia-smi). Also want a curl repro if they can run it from their network.
jordan_eng: Quick reproducible steps for the oncall/support person: 
1) From a host with k8s access: 
   kubectl -n dedicated get pods -o wide > pods.list 
   kubectl -n dedicated logs deployment/serve --since=2h > serve.logs 
   kubectl -n kube-system logs <kubelet-pod> --since=2h > kubelet.logs 
2) On the node(s) that served those reqs (ssh via bastion): 
   sudo dmesg -T | tail -n 200 > dmesg.txt 
   sudo nvidia-smi -q -d MEMORY,UTILIZATION,TEMPERATURE > nvsmi.txt 
   sudo journalctl -u kubelet --since "2 hours ago" > kubelet-journal.txt 
3) Access logs (api-gateway): grep "req_9a1b2" /var/log/gateway/access.log > gateway-reqs.txt 
4) Run collector: sudo /opt/redwood/bin/collect-debug-bundle.sh --trace req_9a1b2c,req_9a1b2d --out /tmp/rd-debug-INC4821.tar.gz 
(collector will include pod logs, node snapshots, nvml output, and request traces)
priya_sre: Also capture: kubectl describe pod <pod-name> for any serve replica that appears in gateway-reqs.txt, and `kubectl get events -n dedicated --sort-by=.metadata.creationTimestamp` to spot OOMs or evictions. If you see Xid or ECC lines in dmesg, flag immediately.
alex_support: Customer shared their local curl (token redacted):
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>" -H "Content-Type: application/json" https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -d '{"model":"redwood-7b","input":"latency test"}' --max-time 30
```
They see 200 sometimes (latency ~18s) and 502 other times.
jordan_eng: For an internal cluster-local repro (safer): 
kubectl exec -it svc/serve-proxy -n dedicated -- 
  curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>" http://serve.local:8080/v1/generate -d '{"input":"latency test"}' -v --max-time 40
eric_oncall: If you collect the bundle and it's large (>200MB) please upload to S3: 
aws s3 cp /tmp/rd-debug-INC4821.tar.gz s3://rd-debug-bundles/INC-4821/ --acl private && then generate presigned url with `aws s3 presign` and paste here. If you can't S3, drop to our secure-share.
alex_support: Pasting sample access log snippet from customer timeframe: 
2026-03-16T11:34:12Z INFO req=req_9a1b2c route=/v1/generate status=200 latency_ms=18500 src=gw-5
2026-03-16T11:34:31Z INFO req=req_9a1b2d route=/v1/generate status=502 backend=serve-3 latency_ms=19000 error=upstream_reset
These line up with their reported timestamps.
priya_sre: Also collect `sudo cat /proc/interrupts | grep -i nv` and `sudo dmesg -T | grep -i "Xid\|ECC"` — GPU Xid codes would push this toward hardware/driver. Include `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=timestamp,name,index,utilization.gpu,utilization.memory,memory.total,memory.used --format=csv` as a CSV snapshot.
ops-bot: deploy/serve v2.1.3 rolled at 2026-03-16T10:58Z by jenkins (build 2345) :white_check_mark:
alex_support: Thanks — I'll coordinate with the customer to run the internal curl and then collect the bundle. Will post the s3 link and the collected artifacts here when ready. If eng needs me to run commands on our side, ping me and I can execute or hand off to oncall.
